question: What is the approximate temperature range of a neutral oxy-acetylene flame?
solution:
The correct answer is __3000°C-3500°C.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A neutral oxy-acetylene flame__ is primarily used for welding.
 
• The flame is produced by mixing oxygen and acetylene in equal proportions.
 
• The flame achieves a temperature range of approximately 3000°C to 3500°C.
 
• This high temperature is ideal for melting and joining metals in various industrial applications.
 
• The neutral flame is characterized by a well-defined inner cone and a bluish outer envelope.
 
• It is suitable for welding low carbon steels, aluminum, and other non-ferrous metals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Carburizing Flame:**

 
 
• Also known as a reducing flame, it contains an excess of acetylene.
 
• It is used for welding high-carbon steel and hard-facing applications.
 
 
 
• **Oxidizing Flame: **
 
 
• Contains an excess of oxygen and is hotter than a neutral flame.
 
• Used for welding brass and brazing operations.
 
 
 
• **Flame Zones:**
 
 
• The inner cone is the hottest part of the flame.
 
• The outer envelope is less hot and primarily provides a protective environment.
